phenotypes: Autism spectrum disorder (ADOS-2 autism, score 8; CARS2-ST 34.5)

clinical.diagnostic_reason: Classified as VUS (ACMG criteria PS2, PP3, BS4); de novo, predicted damaging, but not considered diagnostic

clinical.citation: Large-scale discovery of novel neurodevelopmental disorder-related genes through a unified analysis of single-nucleotide and copy number variants (PMID: 35468861)

variants.description: Recurrent de novo damaging missense variants affecting the same amino acid(s) (specific variants not given in the text)

clinical.diagnostic_reason: Recurrent de novo damaging missense variants at the same amino acid positions in NDD cases, which supports pathogenicity and gene association. KBTBD7 is one of 26 candidate genes.

clinical.citation: An exome sequencing study of Moebius syndrome including atypical cases reveals an individual with CFEOM3A and a TUBB3 mutation (PMID: 28299356)

phenotypes: Moebius syndrome (congenital facial and abducens nerve palsies)

clinical.diagnostic_reason: Not considered diagnostic. The variant was inherited from an unaffected parent, so it was judged unlikely to cause disease. Rare variants in KBTBD7 were shared by two individuals.

model_organism.citation: Wang et al. 2020 - The KBTBD6/7-DRD2 axis regulates pituitary adenoma sensitivity to dopamine agonist treatment (PMID: 32572597)
phenotypes: KBTBD7 KO mice generated by CRISPR-Cas9
Elevated steady-state DRD2 protein in pituitary gland, thalamus, and heart compared to WT mice
Supports KBTBD7 as an E3 ligase adaptor controlling DRD2 degradation in vivo

model_organism.citation: Regulation of Wnt/PCP signaling through p97/VCP-KBTBD7-mediated Vangl ubiquitination and endoplasmic reticulum-associated degradation (PMID: 33990333)
phenotypes: KBTBD7 regulates convergent extension during zebrafish gastrulation (in vivo evidence of a Wnt/PCP-related gastrulation defect upon KBTBD7 perturbation)
Consistent with increased Vangl stability upon KBTBD7 loss

biological.citation: Genau et al. 2015 - CUL3-KBTBD6/KBTBD7 ubiquitin ligase cooperates with GABARAP proteins to spatially restrict TIAM1-RAC1 signaling (PMID: 25684205)
biological.summary: KBTBD6 and KBTBD7 act as substrate adaptors for a CUL3 RING ubiquitin ligase that ubiquitylates TIAM1 (a RAC1 GEF) and targets it for proteasomal degradation. They bind GABARAP proteins through ATG8-interacting motifs, and TIAM1 degradation depends on this binding. Depleting KBTBD6/7 raises RAC1 activity, alters actin morphology, reduces focal adhesions and proliferation, and increases invasion.

biological.citation: Regulation of Wnt/PCP signaling through p97/VCP-KBTBD7-mediated Vangl ubiquitination and endoplasmic reticulum-associated degradation (PMID: 33990333)
biological.summary: KBTBD7 is an E3 ligase recruited by p97/VCP through its UBA-UBX adaptors. It promotes ubiquitination and ERAD of the Wnt/PCP components Vangl1 and Vangl2. In vivo, KBTBD7 regulates convergent extension during zebrafish gastrulation and acts as a tumor suppressor in breast cancer by promoting Vangl degradation.

biological.citation: The KBTBD6/7-DRD2 axis regulates pituitary adenoma sensitivity to dopamine agonist treatment (PMID: 32572597)
biological.summary: A yeast two-hybrid screen identified KBTBD7 as a DRD2-interacting protein. KBTBD6/7 are CUL3 substrate adaptors that ubiquitinate DRD2 at five lysines (K221, K226, K241, K251, K258). KBTBD7 knockout mice had elevated DRD2 in pituitary, thalamus and heart. KBTBD7 is highly expressed in dopamine-resistant prolactinomas, and its knockdown sensitizes cells to cabergoline.

biological.citation: KBTBD7 promotes non-small cell lung carcinoma progression by enhancing ubiquitin-dependent degradation of PTEN (PMID: 35499228)
biological.summary: KBTBD7 is highly expressed in NSCLC tissue compared with paired normal tissue by IHC. Expression correlates with histological type, TNM stage, lymph node metastasis and tumor size. Knockdown reduced NSCLC cell proliferation and invasion. KBTBD7 promotes ubiquitin-dependent PTEN degradation, which activates EGFR/PI3K/AKT signaling.

biological.citation: MicroRNA-21 prevents excessive inflammation and cardiac dysfunction after myocardial infarction through targeting KBTBD7 (PMID: 29991775)
biological.summary: miR-21 directly targets KBTBD7. KBTBD7 interacts with MKK3/6 and promotes their activation, which enhances p38 and NF-κB signaling and DAMP-triggered inflammatory cytokine production in macrophages after MI.

biological.citation: Targeting of ubiquitination and degradation of KLF15 by E3 ubiquitin ligase KBTBD7 regulates LPS-induced septic brain injury in microglia (PMID: 39489209)
biological.summary: KBTBD7 interacts with KLF15 by co-IP and acts as an E3 ligase that ubiquitinates KLF15 for proteasomal degradation. KBTBD7 is upregulated in CLP rat microglia and in LPS-treated microglia. Its knockdown reduces cytokine release and NLRP3/NF-κB activation, and this effect depends on KLF15.

biological.citation: Knockdown of KBTBD7 attenuates septic lung injury by inhibiting ferroptosis and improving mitochondrial dysfunction (PMID: 38652964)
biological.summary: KBTBD7 is highly expressed in LPS-treated human alveolar epithelial cells. Knockdown reduced inflammation, ROS, ferroptosis and mitochondrial dysfunction. KBTBD7 interacts with FOXA1 and promotes its expression, which indirectly represses SLC7A11 transcription. Knockdown also improved lung injury in septic mice.

biological.citation: New TFII-I family target genes involved in embryonic development (PMID: 19527686)
biological.summary: Kbtbd7 (1110008P08Rik) was strongly down-regulated in Gtf2i and Gtf2ird1 mutant mouse embryos, and its promoter has conserved TFII-I binding sites, so it is a likely direct TFII-I target. It encodes a BTB/BACK/Kelch adapter, and its expression pattern suggests a role in brain development. It is a candidate contributor to Williams syndrome.

biological.citation: A transcriptome-wide association study of uterine fibroids to identify potential genetic markers and toxic chemicals (PMID: 36174000)
biological.summary: A TWAS integrating uterine fibroid GWAS data with eQTL data identified KBTBD7 as a novel candidate susceptibility gene for uterine fibroid.

biological.citation: A Robust 8-Gene Prognostic Signature for Early-Stage Non-small Cell Lung Cancer (PMID: 31417870)
biological.summary: KBTBD7 expression was associated with overall survival in early-stage NSCLC across GEO and TCGA cohorts. It is one of eight genes in an independent prognostic risk signature.
biological.sample_size: GSE31210, GSE37745, GSE50081 and TCGA cohorts
